arguments: Unvalidated in/out vector entries are passed to PSA cipher routines
message.text: Unvalidated in/out vector entries are passed to PSA cipher routines

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: valid, the reachable cipher encrypt path passes caller-derived vector entries to the PSA cipher routine without validating the expected input/output vector entries in that path. Evidence: the service call builds vectors from message sizes and only requires at least in_vec[0], the dispatcher only checks in_vec[0].len before dispatching CIPHER, and the encrypt branch reads in_vec[1]/out_vec[0] and calls psa_cipher_encrypt without local entry checks at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:263, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:278, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:291, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:299, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:209, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_init.c:239, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:154, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:158, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:163. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Validate the expected in/out vector count and each used vector before calling PSA routines. Reject NULL bases for nonzero input/output sizes, require adequate output buffer sizes where known, and centralize validation for all SIDs so backend calls never receive malformed pointers from the service boundary.
properties.reasoning: The interface validates vector bases and lengths for the CAN_DO and operation-handle setup/finish/abort paths, but the single-part encrypt path reads in_vec[1] and out_vec[0] directly and passes their base pointers and lengths to psa_cipher_encrypt without checking that the expected vectors are present, that nonzero lengths have non-NULL bases, or that the output vector is writable. In a firmware service boundary, these vectors are derived from the caller message; if malformed vectors can reach this function, the crypto backend may dereference NULL or otherwise invalid service-mapped pointers. Whole-program IPC validation may provide additional guarantees, so the reachability depends on surrounding TF-M vector validation, but this source file itself does not enforce the preconditions it relies on.
